title: A tab after a macro name is dropped, gluing the name to the body
wrong: `#define RE	vec4(1)` becomes `#define REvec4(1)`: the macro RE is no longer defined, and the `RE` in the body refers to nothing.
cause: The `#define` line is re-printed as name + body with the separating whitespace taken from a space-only match, so a tab between them is lost.

title: A function used only from a kept #define is removed, and the names in it renamed
wrong: `#define CALL helper(u)` survives verbatim while `helper` is removed as unused and `u` is renamed to `f`. Expanding CALL then names a function and a variable that the output does not declare.
cause: Unused-function removal and renaming count uses found in the AST; the body of a kept #define is text nothing reads, so its uses are invisible to both.

title: Function reordering lifts both branches of an #ifdef out, defining the function twice
wrong: With a forward declaration present, both `#ifdef A` and `#else` definitions of `g` are pulled out of the region and emitted one after the other, so the output defines `g` twice and the `#ifdef` is left empty.
cause: Function reordering treats the top level as a flat list, so the two alternative definitions look like two ordinary functions to move.

title: A generated name can collide with a preserved external declared later
wrong: A `const float` is renamed to `o` while `out vec4 o;`, declared further down and preserved by the flag, keeps that name. The output declares `o` twice, with different types.
cause: Names are handed out as declarations are reached, and a preserved external is only marked used at its own declaration, so a name it will need is still free before that point.

title: A function called only from a global's initializer is removed as unused
wrong: `float g=f();` keeps its call while `float f()` is removed, so the output calls a function it does not declare.
cause: The call graph is built from function bodies only; a call in a global initializer is not counted.

title: A local's initializer is merged into a call that passes it as an inout argument
wrong: `vec3 v=vec3(0);v=f(v,u);` becomes `vec3 v=f(vec3(0),u);`, passing a constructor to an `inout` parameter. GLSL requires an l-value there, so the output does not compile.
cause: The rule merging a declaration into the assignment that follows checks that the value is pure and used once, but not that the use is in a value position.

title: Argument inlining moves a global into a body where a parameter has its name
wrong: The global passed as the first argument is substituted into the body, where the second parameter is also called `uT` and shadows it. The body then reads the parameter instead of the global and the shader computes a different value.
cause: The substitution checks that the argument is the same at every call site, but not whether the names it reads mean something else at the point it lands.

title: A name declared in both branches of an #if binds to the last declaration alone
wrong: `#ifdef AA float n=1.; #else float n=3.; #endif` is read as one flat list, so both branches are emptied and `n` is inlined as `3.` unconditionally. Under `#define AA` the shader now computes with 3. where the source says 1.
cause: Statement lists ignore conditional directives, so two alternative declarations of one name look like a redeclaration and the uses all bind to the second.

title: A macro the shader tests but never defines can be handed out as a variable name
wrong: A uniform declared under `#ifdef X` is renamed to `X`, producing `uniform float X;` inside `#ifdef X`. An application that defines X to select that branch turns the declaration into `uniform float ;`.
cause: The forbidden-name list holds the macros the file defines; a macro it only tests is not on it.

title: A float literal below ~5e-17 is printed as 0.
wrong: `max(u,1e-20)` becomes `max(u,0.)` and `1.24e-27` becomes `0.`. An epsilon guard or a division by a small constant silently turns into a real zero.
cause: The fixed form keeps at most 16 fraction digits, which are all zero below 5e-17, and it wins the shorter-of-the-two contest against the exponent form.

title: --preserve-externals keeps a uniform's name but renames its struct's fields
wrong: `uniform L light;` keeps `light`, while `struct L{vec3 direction;}` becomes `struct C{vec3 i;}`. An application looking up `light.direction` no longer finds it.
cause: The flag preserves the names of external declarations, but a struct type and its members are renamed independently of the variables that use them.

title: A struct field named like a swizzle component is refused
wrong: `struct S{float q;};` is rejected with "Record field name 'q' is not allowed by Shader Minifier". The field name is legal GLSL and appears in real shaders.
cause: `a.q` is assumed to be a swizzle wherever it appears, so a field of that name would be ambiguous; refusing the file is the current answer.
